All 2025 and 2026 roll calls (6, 23, 102, 145, 190 of 2025; 4, 11, 65, 94 of 2026) were read directly from clerk.house.gov XML. Roll 280 (H.R. 7008) could not be loaded because clerk.house.gov returned 403. The Boyle and Dean Nay votes there come from a search excerpt of the Clerk page; Scanlon's comes from a secondary tracker. Cosponsorships were confirmed through the congress.gov API and govinfo BILLSTATUS XML.
For incumbents with no direct statement, stance is set from the voting record and labeled 'record'. Voter ID is left 'unknown' because the SAVE Act is about proof of citizenship, not photo ID.

Dean and Scanlon are marked 'disagree' on immigration based on their ICE-funding words and Nay votes on the Laken Riley Act. Neither addresses local police cooperation specifically, so the caller may prefer 'unknown'. Boyle is 'mixed' because his votes for the Laken Riley Act differ from his ICE criticism.

term-limits combines term limits and a stock-trading ban. Incumbents' stances reflect stock-ban activity only, and none has a term-limits statement. Dean and Scanlon cosponsored stock bans but voted against the GOP H.R. 7008, which Democrats objected to for exempting the President and grandfathering existing holdings.
smarter.vote wrongly said Boyle introduced H.R. 3115. It is Rep. McBath's bill, and Boyle is not a cosponsor. Dean and Scanlon are.
